name: Non-Cartesian k-space Trajectory & Reconstruction Benchmark
description: We benchmark the current existing methods to jointly learn non-Cartesian k-space trajectory and reconstruction: PILOT, BJORK, and compare them with those obtained from the recently developed generalized hybrid learning (HybLearn) framework. We present the advantages of using projected gradient descent to enforce MR scanner hardware constraints as compared to using added penalties in the cost function. Further, we use the novel HybLearn scheme to jointly learn and compare our results through a retrospective study on fastMRI validation dataset.
evaluation_method: reconstruction-quality metrics (SSIM, PSNR, NMSE), hardware-constraint compliance metrics, and retrospective reconstruction error statistics
general_score_metric: SSIM / PSNR (SSIM commonly reported alongside NMSE)
typical_sota_score: example ranges on fastMRI-like setups: SSIM ~0.85–0.98, PSNR ~30–45 dB, NMSE ~1e-4–1e-2 (varies by acceleration and task)
reputation: A niche but relevant benchmark within the MRI reconstruction research community used to compare joint non-Cartesian trajectory and reconstruction methods; moderate adoption in specialized research groups.
notes: Retrospective study setup and small/heterogeneous datasets can limit generalization; results sensitive to scanner/hardware assumptions and implementation of hardware constraints; non-LLM, domain-specific benchmark.
